subject.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages

question: Should ordinary `claws export` require a complete, exact, corroborated installed state, or should it continue exporting the current portable snapshot without an explicit drift mode?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically implementable, but they promise different reproducibility and recovery semantics to users; tests and CI cannot determine which product contract maintainers intend.

options.title: Exact state by default
options.body: Require healthy exact provenance for normal export and add an explicit snapshot mode that records drift, lineage, dependency digests, and exporter/schema versions.

options.title: Keep snapshot semantics
options.body: Accept the current derivative snapshot behavior as the experimental contract and document that export captures portable current state rather than proving exact installation reproducibility.

options.title: Pause the export slice
options.body: Hold this PR until the RFC and lower lifecycle stack define the complete export, lineage, cron, MCP, and host-rebinding contract together.

recommendation.title: Exact state by default
recommendation.body: Require healthy exact provenance for normal export and add an explicit snapshot mode that records drift, lineage, dependency digests, and exporter/schema versions.

likelyOwner.reason: They articulated the unresolved contract and the concrete exact-state and snapshot alternatives most directly in the current discussion.
